summary:
PR #54 adds exactly Mustafa's three lines to .claude/NIGHT_SHIFT.md (lines 45-47, +3 -0, right after step 6's last line). They match his NS-LINES (a) text byte for byte: sha256 4e3d15658c0afaf40d922cdce9559a8dc2d1079ea04a8fc96e327798b3639223, taken without the final newline, the same way history.md's copy hashes. The PR's live head (REST) is 20f9d59 on base 53272a1, which is current main. One file changed. No guard, hook, settings, script, CI or gate file is touched (git diff --quiet exits 0).

Threat model, for a night run under main's routine guard:
(1) No refusal and no stall. `node .claude/scripts/checkpoint.mjs watch <slug> --every 10 --for 25` is in the guard's plain form. Its program is node, running main's tracked and unchanged script (interpreter() at routine-guard.mjs 989-1013, with protectedInBranch checked at each start). Background runs are refused only for git (753-756). A routine never waits on a prompt: asks and PermissionRequests become denies.
(2) No new kind of background process. The saver already runs in the background. A stint ends itself after 25 minutes plus one last save (checkpoint.mjs 189-211), runs one at a time, stays under the harness's 30-minute default background limit, and still falls under step 8's TaskStop rule.
(3) No stop or handoff check is loosened. The 45-minute busy and handoff thresholds and the FINISH times are unchanged. Only a live model writes the status comment, through update_issue_comment on #16, which the guard already allows (1452). The saver makes no GitHub call, so a cut-off run's status still goes stale and gets handed off.
(4) Two runs on one branch: the risk goes down. This change removes the case where a live run waiting more than 45 minutes looked cut off. Two bounded races remain, both Low, and the saver's never-force and no-code-push rules contain both.
(5) It touches no secrets.

Last night's run (34a2e55, cs/npt-u4f-brief) shows the method working: a stint ended at 00:38 and woke the run while an agent was still running. That run also took `--trailer` from CHECKPOINTS.md §5 (commits 1e97978, 1279cab, 459e436).

findings.what: The lines tie each later stint's start to a fresh status (stint end, then refresh, then next stint), so a stint orphaned by a cut-off ends at most 25 minutes after a refresh, 20 minutes inside the 45-minute handoff. The first stint is not tied to a refresh. It can start when the status is already up to 30 minutes old (step 6's floor). If the run is cut off then, and the cut-off cloud session's background process outlives it (unknown for routines), the orphan saver can keep pushing checkpoint-only commits for up to about 10 minutes after a handoff run has taken the same branch. This is a race, not an exploit. Effect: one side's push is refused as non-fast-forward. The saver never forces and never publishes code, and the handoff run follows CHECKPOINTS §5's 'push refused: fetch and look'. No data is lost. Before this change, the same orphan could live 110 minutes (the default --for), so the change narrows the window.
findings.fix: Accept as is (recommended): a STATUS follow-up at most; it needs no push. To close it fully, step 6's text would have to say to refresh the status before the first stint as well. That rewords his lines, so it is his decision under KIT-FREEZE-2.

findings.where: .claude/NIGHT_SHIFT.md:45 ('While the run waits on agents, nothing else wakes it'); evidence of the working case: git show 34a2e55:.checkpoints/npt-u4f-brief.md lines 94-106
findings.what: The wake-up works when the run sits idle waiting on background agents. Last night's run shows this: its stint ended at 00:38 and woke the run while netcode-architect ran to 00:48. A run blocked inside one foreground Agent or workflow call is likely not woken by a stint's end, because the harness reports a background task's end between turns (not verified inside a routine). Its status can then still pass 45 minutes, and a later hourly run could hand off onto a branch that a live run still holds. This was already true before the change: step 6's 30-minute rule cannot be met in that case either. The change neither creates nor widens it, and the saver's never-force rule still bounds the effect.
findings.fix: Accept for this PR. If wanted later, a separate kit line such as 'while the saver runs in stints, launch agents in the background' would close it. That would be his decision under KIT-FREEZE-2. It adds a line and does not reword his three.

to_mustafa:
The three lines in the pull request are exactly the ones you said yes to; their fingerprint (sha256) matches. Nothing else changed: no guard, hook, settings, script or CI file. For the night shift this is safe. The new saver command is one the night's guard already allows. It stops by itself after 25 minutes, so it never waits on you and never leaves a long-running process behind. It also makes the night-run mix-up less likely: before, a night run waiting on agents for over 45 minutes looked cut off, and the next hourly run could take over its branch while it was still working. Two small leftover races remain, both rated Low. Both end at worst with one save refused, never with lost work or published code. I recommend accepting both as they are; neither needs a new push.

Decisions needed:
1. SA-NS-1 (the first saver stint): your lines refresh the status before every later stint, but not before the first one. If a run is cut off just after starting it, its saver could overlap a handoff run by up to about 10 minutes, and one side's checkpoint save would then be refused. Options: (a) accept it (recommended: before this change the overlap could last 110 minutes); (b) reword your step-6 text later so the first stint also starts right after a status refresh (that changes your lines, under the kit freeze).
2. SA-NS-2 (foreground agents): the stint's end wakes a night run only when its agents run in the background, as last night's did. A run stuck inside one long foreground agent call can still look cut off after 45 minutes. This was already the case before the change. Options: (a) accept it for now (recommended); (b) a later kit change adds a separate line: launch agents in the background while the saver runs in stints.

For Mustafa:
1. When the advisor has approved head 20f9d59918eea1e3431ae830f72510f83f6424c7, give your go (or not) on merging pull request #54 at that head.
2. After the merge, a night item whose branch was made before the merge can't be resumed at night until that branch takes main in. The guard refuses the switch safely; it is the usual effect of any kit merge.
